messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: I added to the pedantic mode page
parts:
[back on stan-dev]

> On Jun 25, 2016, at 9:30 AM, Andrew Gelman <gel...@stat.columbia.edu> wrote:
>
> See here:
> https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Stan-Parser-Pedantic-Mode

Thanks. That looks great.

If the messages are that long, we need to be able to turn them off.
Yes, definitely keep them on by default.

We want to be able to do this anyway for our other warnings.

I like the no-indent warning.

But now we're crossing the line not from program warnings to
general stats and formatting advice, which is going to annoy a lot
of people if we can't turn it off. So maybe a lint mode that
you have to turn on that includes things like indentation vs.
the hardcore uniform() warnings about constraints vs. uniform()
without Andrew's preferred bounds.

- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] I added to the pedantic mode page
parts:
I was thinking of “pedantic” as in the pedantic C++
compiler option, hence my thinking of it being done
in the parser. An added benefit of this approach is
that it would allow us to turn it on by default and force
users to turn it off.

But a lint-like system would be good, too.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] I added to the pedantic mode page
parts:
Yup --- that's what I understood you to mean.
That'd be things like not defining variables before
they're used and not having constraints on parameters
used in uniform distributions and the like.

Crossing over into style, like which priors to
use and whether to include spaces, passes into lint
territory. Arguably the Jacobian warnings are also
in this category in that they're not ill-formed
programs, they just might not do what the user expects.

- Bob
